To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the resonant contribution to the curvature perturbation power spectrum, after the turn, is smaller than the previous estimates by a factor of order 2, that the resonant effect is dominated by the coupling between the light direction and the heavy direction at the instant of turn and that the direct coupling between these two directions is not significant after the turn.

the resonant effect of the oscillatory modes on the power spectra of the light and heavy fields is of order 10−2 and 10−3 respectively, whereas the direct coupling between light and heavy modes is of order 1.

(i) the effect of the heavy modes on the power spectra of the light field is negligible; (ii) the resonant effect on the power spectrum is subdominant compared to the direct coupling effect, but it is still significant; (iii) the resonant enhancement of the power spectrum is not limited to the scales corresponding to the turn but extends to all scales, with a maximum at scales of the order of the turn frequency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a more accurate description of the impact of massive modes on the curvature power spectrum produced in the context of a two-field inflationary model with a sharp turn.
the effect of massive modes on the curvature power spectrum produced after the sudden turn of the trajectory of the inflaton in the two-field inflationary scenario.
the impact of the background oscillations and of the direct coupling on the power spectrum after the turn of the inflation trajectory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of two-fields inflation, the resonant effect dominates the direct coupling effect.

the oscillatory features in the power spectrum are due to the resonant effect and the direct coupling between light and heavy modes, but with the former being dominant and the latter being subdominant.

the resonant effect is subdominant with respect to the direct coupling between light and heavy modes, but that the resonant contribution is still significant, especially in the case of a turn with a large angle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of a two-field model, the resonant effect is the dominant one and that the effect of the coupling between light and heavy modes is subdominant.
the oscillatory features in the power spectrum after a sharp turn of the inflation trajectory is mainly due to the coupling between the light direction and the heavy direction at the instant of turn.
the resonant effect is subleading compared to the direct coupling between light and heavy modes, and the latter is also subleading to the effect of the background curvature oscillations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resonant effect is not the dominant source of oscillations in the curvature power-spectrum after a turn.

, in the mass basis where the light and heavy degrees of freedom are decoupled, the oscillatory features due to the resonant coupling are suppressed with respect to those obtained in the field basis where the light mode is directly coupled to the heavy mode.
the resonant effect is subleading compared to the direct coupling between light and heavy modes.
